:: COMMON JUDGMENT ::

The petitions filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor vehicles Act are clubbed together as they are arising out of the same accident and the cause of action in all the three cases is one and the same.
2. The brief facts of the petitioners are as under:
SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.3746/2022, 3747/2022 & MVC No.3748/2022 It is the case of the petitioners that on 07.03.2021 at around 3.30 pm., when the petitioner in MVC No. 3747/2022 was riding his two wheeler bearing reg.No.KA-41-H-5211 along with pillion riders i.e., petitioner in MVC No.3746/2022 and MVC No.3748/2022 from Hassan side towards Bengaluru side on NH-75, Hassan - Nelamangala main road at Avaragere gate, Yadiyuru Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumakuru District, at that time, the driver of a Car bearing reg.No.KA-51-P-9778 came from Hassan side towards Bengaluru side in a very high speed with rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's two wheeler from back side and caused the accident.
Due to impact, all the petitioners fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, all the petitioners were shifted to CHC, Kunigal after first aid petitioner in MVC No.3747/2022 was shifted to MM Hospital, Kunigal wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and petitioner in MVC 3746/2022 and petitioner in MVC No. SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.3746/2022, 3747/2022 & MVC No.3748/2022 3748/2022 were shifted to A.C.Giri Hospital, Belluru wherein they took treatment as an inpatient.
All of them have spent huge amount towards medical expenses.

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, petitioner in MVC No.3746/2022 was aged about 12 Years and was a bright student.
The petitioner in MVC No.3747/2022 was aged about 36 years and was doing labour work and earning more than Rs.20,000/- per month.
The petitioner in MVC No.3748/2022 was aged about 32 years and was doing labour work and earning more than Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to fracture injury, all the petitioner were completely disabled and suffering with deformity.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Car bearing reg.No.KA-51-P- 9778.
The Amruthuru police registered a crime against the driver of the offending Car in crime No.0030/2021 under Section 279, 337 of IPC.

Therefore,
the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.3746/2022,
3747/2022 & MVC No.3748/2022 severally liable to pay the compensation.

Hence,
they have prayed to allow their petition.
3. The summons in all the cases have been duly served on the respondent No.1 and 2.
The respondent No.1 has not appeared before the tribunal in all the cases.
Hence, the respondent No.1 has been placed exparte in all the cases.
4. The respondent No.2 has appeared before this Tribunal in all the cases and filed its written statement.
It has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the same is liable to be dismissed in limine.
It has contended that, the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, the policy has become null and void and the contract of insurance entered between the insurers and insured cannot be enforceable.
Further insured vehicle had no FC as on the date of alleged accident.
SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.3746/2022, 3747/2022 & MVC No.3748/2022 Further contended that, the car is not involved in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner.
The petitioner sustained injuries due to fall from motor cycle bearing No.KA-41-H-5211 which he was pillion riding with two pillion riders.
Further contended that, petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties to the petition and also petition is barred by limitation.
With these contentions he had prayed to dismiss the petition in all the cases.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW-1 to 3.
I have perused the entire cross-examination of PW-1 to 3 and they have denied that accident occurred due to the rider of the motor cycle.
Therefore, the learned counsel for the Respondent No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW.1 to 3 to disbelieve their version.
12. On the other hand, though the respondent No.2 has taken up several contentions but he has not stepped into witness box to adduce any evidence.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective in nature.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.3746/2022, 3747/2022 & MVC No.3748/2022 negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing reg.No.KA-51-MP-9778 which belongs to respondent No.2.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative in all the cases.

In view of discussion made while answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the minor petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during the treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
14. The natural guardian/father of minor SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.3746/2022, 3747/2022 & MVC No.3748/2022 petitioner has contended that due to accident his son sustained grievous injuries.
In order to prove the injuries caused to him, he has produced Ex.P.21 wound certificate and Ex.P.22 discharge summary.

abrasion over the right back, multiple small abrasion over the right lower limb, abrasion over the left shoulder and lacerated wound over the forehead and also doctor opines that all the injuries are simple in nature.
As per Ex.P.22 - discharge summary issued by Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research centre which discloses that, he took treatment from 07.03.2021 to 10.03.2021 i.e., for 4 days.
It is relevant note that the petitioner has not examined doctor to show the degree of his disability caused due to the accident.
Absolutely there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner is having permanent disability due to the accident.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:

Learned counsel for petitioner argued that in regard to interest, the interest has to be consider as 8% and relied the citation in 2018 ACJ 535, but the Hon'ble Apex court of India in AIR 2006 SC 3026 Manalal Prabhudayal V/s Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd,
wherein it is held that, It is well settled that award of interest is in the discretion of court.

entities.text: AIR 2006 SC 3026 Manalal Prabhudayal V/s Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Normally, when interest is granted, appellate, revisional or writ court would not interfere with exercise of discretion unless the discretion has been exercised arbitrarily or capriciousley.

It is equally well settled that like grant of interest, rate of interest is also in the discretion of the court and in the absence of any agreement between the parties, usually, the court would not interfere with rate of interest unless it is convinced that the direction of the lower court was ex facie bad in law.
Hence
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Car.
Hence, Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners in all the cases.
The primary liability is on Respondent No.2 to pay aforesaid award amount to the petitioners respectively together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 in the 'Partly affirmative' in all the cases.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
It has contended that, the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further contended that, the policy has become null and void and the contract of insurance entered between the insurers and insured cannot be enforceable.
Learned counsel for petitioner argued that in regard to interest, the interest has to be consider as 8% and relied the citation in 2018 ACJ 535, but the Hon'ble Apex court of India in AIR 2006 SC 3026 Manalal Prabhudayal V/s Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd,
wherein it is held that, It is well settled that award of interest is in the discretion of court.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective in nature.
Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.3746/2022, 3747/2022 & MVC No.3748/2022 negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing reg.No.KA-51-MP-9778 which belongs to respondent No.2.

In the instant case the petitioner has not examined doctor to prove the degree of his disability.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to that effect, this Tribunal is not inclined to accept the version of the petitioner that he is having permanent disability caused in the accident.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities of life on account of permanent disability.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for medical bills of Rs.16,704/-.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.7,20,000/- (Rs.15,000/- X 12 X 16 X 25/100) towards loss of future income on the account of disability of the petitioner.
Normally, when interest is granted, appellate, revisional or writ court would not interfere with exercise of discretion unless the discretion has been exercised arbitrarily or capriciousley.
It is equally well settled that like grant of interest, rate of interest is also in the discretion of the court and in the absence of any agreement between the parties, usually, the court would not interfere with rate of interest unless it is convinced that the direction of the lower court was ex facie bad in law.
Hence
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Car.
